excerpt: Prices, hours and how to reserve your time slot for Edward James's Surrealist Garden in Xilitla, plus the entry tips that keep you from losing your turn.
contentHtml:
Las Pozas tickets are your way into Edward James's Surrealist Garden in Xilitla, San Luis Potosí, one of the most unusual sculptural works in Mexico. The most common question travelers have is whether they can buy admission at the ticket window on the same day or need to book ahead—and the answer changes your whole plan. Going about your Las Pozas tickets the wrong way can leave you without a time slot, so it's worth reading this before you head out.

Las Pozas tickets: quick facts

Admission$180 MXN per adult; $120 MXN for children ages 6 to 12 and seniors over 65; kids under 6, free
Mandatory guide$30 MXN per person in Spanish; $60 MXN in another language
HoursOpen Wednesday through Monday from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., with last entry at 4:00 p.m.; closed on Tuesdays.
How to payYou reserve your time slot for free on the official system (up to 60 days ahead) and pay at the ticket window on the day of your visit, in cash or by card. Arrive 10 minutes early: if you're late, you lose your slot.
Getting thereAn hour and a half by car from Ciudad Valles; the garden is in Xilitla
TourSurrealist Route: from $1,400 MXN per person, 8 to 10 h, with transportation from your lodging in Xilitla or Ciudad Valles ($400 MXN extra per booking from Valles)

How much are Las Pozas tickets, and what do they include?

General admission and special rates in 2026

Admission to Edward James's Surrealist Garden costs $180 MXN per adult in 2026. Children ages 6 to 12 and adults 65 and older pay $120 MXN, and children under 6 get in free. None of these rates include the guide, which is mandatory to enter the garden.

Travelers we work with often ask whether they can explore the garden on their own: the answer is no. Visits are only allowed with authorized guides, who cost $30 MXN per person in Spanish or $60 MXN in another language, and the tour lasts an hour and a half. Book the Surrealist Route, with admission included, to avoid unexpected charges at the ticket window.

Tours from Ciudad Valles: the all-inclusive option

If you'd rather go with a guide, the Surrealist Route, which visits Edward James's Las Pozas with transportation from your lodging in Xilitla or Ciudad Valles ($400 MXN extra per booking from Valles), breakfast, admission fees and a certified guide, costs $1,400 MXN per person. It bundles transportation, guide and admission into one payment, which simplifies logistics, especially for families.

You can round out the day with our guide to the best restaurants in Xilitla.

Opening hours and entry tips you should know

What are the official hours of Edward James's garden?

The garden is open from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Wednesday through Monday, with last entry at 4:00 p.m. It's closed on Tuesdays. The groups we bring every season know that arriving before 10:00 a.m. guarantees better light for photos and smaller crowds.

One thing we repeat on all our tours: arrive 10 minutes before your time slot, because if you're late you lose it. It's one of the most important entry tips you can take away from this article. See available tours in the Huasteca Potosina, with schedules handled for you to avoid this problem.

Where and how do you buy Las Pozas tickets?

For now there are no online sales: you reserve your time slot for free on the official system (up to 60 days ahead) and pay at the garden's ticket window on the day of your visit, in cash or by card. If you see $170 MXN on other websites: that was the online price in early 2026.

We recommend planning your visit at least 48 hours ahead on weekends and during vacation periods. To organize your whole stay, see the perfect 3-day Xilitla itinerary we put together with tested routes.

Practical tips before visiting Edward James's garden

  • Reserve your time slot ahead of time: the reservation is free and made on the official system up to 60 days ahead; Las Pozas tickets are paid at the garden's ticket window on the day of your visit, in cash or by card.
  • Stick to your time slot: arrive 10 minutes early, because if you're late you lose it. This is the number-one entry tip nobody forgets after losing their slot.
  • Plan ahead if you're visiting with kids: The garden is family-friendly, but the paths are uneven. See our guide to Xilitla with kids to adapt the visit.
  • The right clothes and shoes: Wear closed-toe shoes with non-slip soles. The ground is often wet near the garden's waterfalls.

Frequently asked questions about Las Pozas tickets

Can you buy Las Pozas tickets at the entrance on the same day?

You pay there, at the ticket window at the garden's entrance, on the day of your visit, in cash or by card, but first you have to reserve your time slot, for free, on the official system (up to 60 days ahead). For now there are no online sales. Arrive 10 minutes early: if you're late, you lose your slot.

How much is admission to Edward James's garden in 2026?

Admission is $180 MXN per adult. Children ages 6 to 12 and adults 65 and older pay $120 MXN, and children under 6 get in free. The mandatory guide costs an extra $30 MXN per person in Spanish, or $60 MXN in another language. For now there are no online sales: you reserve your time slot for free on the official system (up to 60 days ahead) and pay at the garden's ticket window on the day of your visit, in cash or by card.

How do you get to Edward James's garden from Ciudad Valles?

From Ciudad Valles, the drive to Xilitla takes an hour and a half. You can also go with us: the Surrealist Route, which visits Edward James's Las Pozas with transportation from your lodging in Xilitla or Ciudad Valles ($400 MXN extra per booking from Valles), breakfast, admission fees and a certified guide, costs $1,400 MXN per person.

Is Las Pozas a safe visit with kids or as a couple?

Yes, the garden is well suited to families and couples. As an entry tip, wear closed-toe, non-slip shoes and stay within the areas marked by the authorized guides. The Huasteca Potosina has well-established tourism infrastructure around Xilitla for all kinds of travelers.
